summary: Ten comment-endorsed discoveries spanning CAD, AI, email, molecular biology, music, history, and hardware protection.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: SolveSpace
items.source_story_title: Show HN: SolidCraft – Open-Source Parametric CAD in Rust (With MCP Support)
items.summary: Open-source parametric CAD praised for reliable sketching and a coherent, compact interface.
items.why_included: A longtime user explicitly prefers its polished core over broader but frustrating CAD alternatives.
items.evidence: A longtime user calls SolveSpace stable, fast, and compact, and says it remains their go-to for practical work.

evidence_sources.author: rspeele
evidence_sources.excerpt: SolveSpace -- pretty stable and reliable. Fast, compact, great sketching interface, good discoverable UI.

items.name: P4Merge
items.summary: Visual diff and merge tool endorsed for resolving conflicts in Git workflows.
items.why_included: Specific praise for the merge tool survives the commenter's criticism of Perforce itself.
items.evidence: A commenter who used P4Merge with Git describes it as an outstanding manual merge tool.

evidence_sources.author: pyrolistical
evidence_sources.excerpt: If I were still manually merging conflicts the p4merge tool was GOAT I used it in git

items.name: Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google's AI model praised by an internal user for clear, organized answers.
items.why_included: The comment independently endorses the submitted model and identifies a concrete writing preference.
items.evidence: A commenter reports internal use at Google and prefers Argon's direct, organized phrasing over Opus 5.5.

evidence_sources.author: asdfman123
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using it for a while internally at Google. I prefer Argon over Opus 5.5 because of the clear thinking and directness. It phrases things in an organized, straightforward way.

items.name: Whisper
items.source_story_title: We turned EmbeddingGemma 2 into a speech-to-text model
items.summary: Open-source speech recognition praised for GPU-accelerated transcription without sending audio off-device.
items.why_included: An explicit positive firsthand report highlights a practical local transcription alternative.
items.evidence: A user reports great results with GPU-accelerated Whisper while keeping all processing on their machine.

evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Whisper with great results; GPU acceleration gets the job done, nothing leaves my box, and the medium model is overkill.

items.name: Aqua Mail
items.summary: Customizable Android email client recommended by a longtime user; paid licensing is a caveat.
items.why_included: A concrete phone-email recommendation includes both sustained approval and a pricing drawback.
items.evidence: A longtime user calls Aqua Mail solid and highly customizable, recommends it for heavy phone-email use, and flags its changed payment model.

evidence_sources.author: jdoss
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's been solid and it is super customizable. I think the only downside is they changed their payment model a while back and if you didn't buy it back then it costs monthly fee or a $99.99 for a lifetime license. I highly recomend it if you do a lot of email on your phone.

items.name: Guitoro
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Guitoro, a virtual guitar you strum with your keyboard
items.summary: Keyboard-strummed virtual guitar praised for intuitive design; custom tunings remain a requested feature.
items.why_included: An experienced guitarist independently praises the app while identifying a specific limitation.
items.evidence: A guitarist calls the app intuitive and exceptionally well designed but cannot find their nonstandard tunings.

evidence_sources.author: slinkydink
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been playing for years, and so happy to see an app so intuitive. The only thing is that I use several non standard tunings none of them are found in the drop down.....

items.name: The Machinery of Life
items.source_story_title: The baffling intelligence of a single cell (2024)
items.summary: David Goodsell's illustrated biology book recommended for patient, visual explanations of cellular machinery.
items.why_included: A reader directly recommends the book rather than merely mentioning the author or article.
items.evidence: A reader strongly recommends The Machinery of Life for its patient, visual explanation of cellular mechanisms.

evidence_sources.author: ORDINAND_PIZZA
evidence_sources.excerpt: i've read and can highly recommend his book The Machinery of Life for a patient and visual explanation of these baffling machines!

items.name: LifeBrush
items.source_story_title: The baffling intelligence of a single cell (2024)
items.summary: Open-source VR molecular painting and simulation system praised for making cellular illustrations interactive.
items.why_included: Detailed praise for manipulating molecular scenes offers an unusual hands-on science discovery.
items.evidence: A commenter praises LifeBrush's interactive ribosome scenes, where users can move a ribosome rather than wait for Brownian motion.

evidence_sources.author: DonHopkins
evidence_sources.excerpt: The interaction is the magic: in the overview, a ribosome moves along mRNA as tRNA brings amino acids and a polypeptide chain grows. You can grab the ribosome and move it where you want, rather than wait for Brownian motion.

items.name: The History Blog
items.source_story_title: Hittite royal archive found in Turkey
items.summary: History publication praised for detailed, nonsensational reporting with source material and pictures.
items.why_included: An explicit endorsement identifies a useful reading destination beyond the submitted archaeology story.
items.evidence: A commenter praises The History Blog's seriousness, accessible detail, close-to-primary sources, and pictures.

evidence_sources.author: sherr
evidence_sources.excerpt: The History Blog is a small gem because it is serious and not sensational. Always with a good level of detail for the average interested visitor, and from the original (or close by) sources. Plus pictures.

items.name: Master Bond tamper-resistant potting compounds
items.source_story_title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
items.summary: Electronics encapsulation compounds praised for resisting destructive tampering; cost is the trade-off.
items.why_included: A hardware practitioner's concrete positive experience is more useful than generic wallet-security speculation.
items.evidence: A practitioner identifies Master Bond as a brand used in tamper-exposed devices and reports no known intact-circuit epoxy removal, while warning about cost.

evidence_sources.author: jacquesm
evidence_sources.excerpt: The devices we made were put in places where there was a significant risk of tampering and to the best of my knowledge nobody ever managed to break the epoxy bond to the point that the circuit was still functional. But as I wrote above: not cheap.
